lines.en: I am so sorry I forgot to call you yesterday, Max.
lines.pt: Sinto muito ter esquecido de ligar para você ontem, Max.

lines.en: You don’t have to apologise, Ada. I knew you were busy.

lines.en: I had to work late, but I wanted to call you.

lines.en: Friends don’t have to call every day. We can talk this weekend.

lines.en: Do I have to bring anything to your party on Saturday?

lines.en: No, you don’t have to bring food. I have already cooked a lot.

lines.en: Then I will bring some music. You don’t have to say yes, but I want to help.
lines.pt: Então vou trazer um pouco de música. Você não precisa dizer sim, mas quero ajudar.

lines.en: No, I don’t have to work on Sunday, so I can stay late.
lines.pt: Não, não preciso trabalhar no domingo, então posso ficar até tarde.

lines.en: Perfect. And you don’t have to wear anything special. It is only friends.
lines.pt: Perfeito. E você não precisa usar nada especial. São só amigos.

lines.en: Thanks, Max. With you, I never have to worry.
lines.pt: Obrigada, Max. Com você, eu nunca preciso me preocupar.

teach.goal: Ponte português → inglês com palavras úteis.
solo: Peça uma frase pessoal com 2 das palavras.
group: Palavras: invitation, guest, favor, argument, secret, worry.
Aluno diz em português um uso real, depois a palavra em inglês.
extra90: Cada aluno escolhe a palavra mais útil e explica por quê.

facts.label: Don’t have to
facts.sub: Não é necessário: don’t have to. Pergunta: Do I have to…? Passado: had to / didn’t have to. Mustn’t proíbe.

facts.label: Não precisa
facts.sub: Use don’t have to quando algo não é necessário: You don’t have to bring food. Não é proibição! Com he/she, diga doesn’t have to: She doesn’t have to call. Depois vem o verbo simples.

facts.label: Eu preciso…?
facts.sub: Para perguntar se algo é necessário, use do + have to: Do I have to bring anything? Do you have to leave early? É uma pergunta educada entre amigos.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Don’t have to means it is not necessary.
Don’t have to means it is forbidden.
“Do I have to bring anything?” is a polite question.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Don’t have to means it is not necessary. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Don’t have to means it is forbidden. → Falso (That is mustn’t.)
“Do I have to bring anything?” is a polite question. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Friends who forgive fast · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Friday evening in a busy part of Chicago. Ada walks fast along the river with her bag. She sees her old friend Max near the bridge. Max has an invitation for a party on Saturday. Ada wants to say she is sorry about yesterday. Good friends often solve a small problem in a minute.
“I am so sorry I forgot to call you yesterday, Max.” says Ada. “You don’t have to apologise, Ada. I knew you were busy.” says Max. “I had to work late, but I wanted to call you.” says Ada.
